note: Cross-platform KAT for the v3 BLINDED PSK advertisement. WIRE_SPEC 3.3.1. Replaces the static lc_hex(SHA-256(psk)) fingerprint, which was identical on every call between the same pair and therefore a permanent per-relationship correlator for the relay, and the parallel pskRoles array, which told the relay which pairs had met in person. Generated by tools/kat/gen_psk_advert_v3_kat.py -- edit the generator, never this file.

algorithm.tag_preimage: ASCII "qa-psk-advert-v3" (16 B) || u8(len(call_id_utf8)) || call_id_utf8 || nonce_sender (32 B) || u8(role)
algorithm.nonce: SHA-256( ASCII "qa-psk-advert-nonce-v3" (22 B) || u8(len(call_id_utf8)) || call_id_utf8 || sender_ephemeral_x25519_pub (32 B) )
algorithm.nonce_source: DERIVED, never sent. sender_ephemeral_x25519_pub is the sender's own ephemeral X25519 public key as it appears in the SIGNED bundle: OFFER `x25519PublicKey`, ACCEPT `ciphertext.x25519`. Both are already bound by the v2 transcript (offerV2 binds lp(x25519PublicKey), acceptV2 binds lp(ctX25519)), so the nonce is authenticated with no new wire field and no transcript change. A nonce sent as a plain unsigned field would be a silent PSK-downgrade oracle: flip a byte, nothing matches, the PSK drops out of the session key, the call still connects.
algorithm.role_on_wire: NOT on the wire. Folded into the tag preimage by the sender; the receiver recovers it by computing each local key's tag under every role 0..255 and seeing which value matches. The full byte range, not just the defined roles: a role disagreement between the two sides must not cost the PSK, and a role added later must interoperate with an older build without a lockstep release. Cost is 256*m HMAC-SHA256 for m local keys -- microseconds.
algorithm.advEnc_shape: UNCHANGED: u8(m) || (u8(role) || 32B)*m. The 32-byte tag occupies the slot the 32-byte fingerprint had, and pskRoles=null already encodes as all-zero role bytes, so the existing signature covers the advertisement byte-for-byte with no format change on any platform.
algorithm.match_rule: first tag in the RECEIVED order that any local key reproduces under any role wins -- received order in the OUTER loop, so the advertiser keeps the priority
algorithm.match_nonce: the SENDER's nonce, never the receiver's own
algorithm.static_fingerprint_still_local: lc_hex(SHA-256(psk)) remains the LOCAL identifier off the wire: vault keys, kc_mac mixedFingerprints, PSK-mix mixId, UI, the hw_only D4 intersect. A receiver MUST translate a matched tag back to its own static fingerprint before handing it downstream, or those consumers silently see an unknown value.

nonce_vectors.name: accept-leg-different-ephemeral
nonce_vectors.note: on the ACCEPT leg the sender's ephemeral is `ciphertext.x25519`, so the two legs of ONE call derive different nonces and advertise unrelated tags.

nonce_vectors.name: different-call-same-ephemeral
nonce_vectors.note: binds the nonce to the call as well, so a replayed ephemeral in another call still yields fresh tags.

nonce_vectors.name: empty-call-id
nonce_vectors.note: length-prefixed, so an empty call_id is well defined, not ambiguous.

nonce_vectors.name: non-ascii-call-id
nonce_vectors.note: the length prefix counts UTF-8 BYTES, not characters. An implementation that prefixes the character count diverges here and nowhere else.

tag_vectors.name: nfc-role-1-same-key-and-nonce
tag_vectors.note: identical key and nonce to the previous vector, role differs -> a wholly different tag. This is what keeps the role off the wire.

tag_vectors.name: same-key-different-nonce
tag_vectors.note: the unlinkability property: one key, two calls, unrelated tags.

tag_vectors.name: non-ascii-call-id
tag_vectors.note: same UTF-8-bytes-not-characters trap as the nonce vectors.

tag_vectors.name: role-255-upper-bound
tag_vectors.note: the top of the search space the receiver walks.

match_vectors.name: advertiser-priority-first-received-match-wins
match_vectors.note: psk_2 is advertised FIRST and we hold both, so received index 0 wins. Iterating local keys in the outer loop would return psk_1 and move the priority from the advertiser to the receiver -- the v1 `?.sorted()` bug.

match_vectors.name: role-recovered-not-assumed
match_vectors.note: THE point of the 256-wide search. We hold the material with no idea how the peer labelled it; the peer sent role=2, and matching recovers 2. A receiver that only tried its own recorded role would find nothing here and silently drop a PSK the two sides genuinely share.

match_vectors.name: role-255-recovered
match_vectors.note: the upper bound is inside the search space, not one past it.

match_vectors.name: wrong-nonce-never-matches
match_vectors.note: matching MUST use the SENDER's nonce. Using our own is the mistake that makes two v3 peers silently fail to find a key they both hold.

match_vectors.name: legacy-v2-static-fingerprints-do-not-match
match_vectors.note: what a v3 receiver sees from a pre-v3 peer: lc_hex(SHA-256(psk)) is not a tag under any role, so the result is a clean no-match rather than a wrong match. The caller must then say so out loud -- silently deriving without the PSK is the failure mode to avoid.

match_vectors.name: second-received-tag-matches
match_vectors.note: the walk does not stop at the first miss.
